# Lesson 2: Sometimes geometry is enough[, until it's not]{.fragment}

## {style="text-align:center;"}
### _XKCD 2807 Bad Map Projection Abs(Longitude)_
![](comics/bad/xkcd-2807-bad_map_projection_abs_longitude_2x.png)

##
```r
get_hemisphere <- function(central_meridian = 0, density = 1) {
  lons <- c( 1,  1, -1, -1,  1) * 90 + central_meridian
  lats <- c(-1,  1,  1, -1, -1) * 90
  st_polygon(list(matrix(c(lons, lats), ncol = 2))) |>
    st_sfc() |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    st_as_sf(crs = 4326) |>
    smoothr::densify(density)
}
hemi_w <- get_hemisphere(-90)
hemi_e <- get_hemisphere(90)

world_w <- World |>
  st_intersection(hemi_w) |>
  mutate(geometry = geometry * matrix(c(-1, 0, 0, 1), 2, 2)) |>
  st_set_crs(4326)

world_e <- World |>
  st_intersection(hemi_e)

world_abs <- world_w |>
  bind_rows(world_e) |>
  mutate(id = 1) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise() |>
  mutate(geometry = geometry - c(90, 0)) |>
  st_set_crs(4326) |>
  st_transform("+proj=eqearth")
```

## {style="text-align:center"}
![](my-abs-longitude.png){fig-align="center"}

## {style="text-align:center;"}
### _XKCD 1500 Upside-Down Map_
![](comics/bad/xkcd-1500-upside_down_map_2x.png)

## {style="font-size:120%"}
```r
world_upside_down <- World |>
  mutate(
    geometry = geometry * diag(c(-1, 2, 2))) |>
  st_set_crs(4326) |>
  st_transform("+proj=eqearth")

ggplot(world_upside_down) +
  geom_sf() +
  theme_minimal()
```

## {style="text-align:center;"}
![](my-upside-down-map.png){fig-align="center"}

## Supplementary lesson {style="text-align:center;"}
### Sometimes, you _have to lie_ about your data's projection


# Lesson 3: Mercator is more useful than you think[, and never not funny]{.fragment}

## {style="text-align:center"}
### _XKCD 2489 Bad Map Projection: The Greenland Special_
![](comics/bad/xkcd-2489-bad_map_projection_the_greenland_special_2x.png)

##
```r
greenland <- World |>
  filter(name == "Greenland") |>
  st_transform("+proj=merc") |>
  mutate(geometry = 
    (geometry + c(2e6, -3.1e6)) * diag(1, 2, 2) * 0.85) |>
  st_set_crs("+proj=merc")

greenland_buffer <- greenland |>
  st_buffer(1e5)

w <- World |>
  st_transform("+proj=moll") |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_set_crs("+proj=merc") |>
  st_difference(greenland_buffer) |>
  bind_rows(greenland)
```

## {style="text-align:center"}
![](my-greenland-special.png)

## {style="text-align:center"}
### _XKCD 2613 Bad Map Projection: Madagascator_
![](comics/bad/xkcd-2613-bad_map_projection_madagascator_2x.png)

##
```r
ll <- c(-4.595750619515433, 55.43837198904654)
madagascator <- World |>
  st_transform(str_glue("+proj=laea +lon_0={ll[2]} +lat_0={ll[1]}")) |>
  st_set_crs("+proj=laea +lon_0=150 +lat_0=90") |>
  st_transform("+proj=merc")
```

## {style="text-align:center;"}
![](my-madagascator.png)

## Supplementary lessons {style="text-align:center;"}
### Azimuthal projections are your friend
### Antarctica is a menace: sometimes you just have to ditch it

# Lesson learned

##
### Sometimes, you need a drawing package
### Sometimes geometry is enough, until it's not
### Mercator is more useful than you think, and never not funny
### If a job's worth doing, it's worth doing well, unless it's not

##
### Sometimes, you _have to lie_ about your data's projection
### Azimuthal projections are your friend
### Antarctica is a menace: sometimes you just have to ditch it

## Finally
### All projections are wrong... 
### ...some are amusing{.fragment}
